research_scope: Independent Wave2 source-free cross-formulation prerequisite judgments; no outside source research, new mathematical meanings, source rewrites, production comparisons or certification.

aliases.reason: The Dedekind-domain factorization characterization requires a finite iterated product P_1⋯P_n of ideals with the same finite-sums-of-products construction as the binary ideal product IJ, including R as the empty product. The conditions that the factors are nonzero prime ideals, and that factorization is unique, belong only to the Dedekind characterization; aliasing does not make an arbitrary product prime or unique.

The locally-ringed-space definition uses the stalk O_{X,x} at every point x, which is precisely the sheaf-theoretic filtered colimit of sections on neighborhoods used in the reduced-scheme source's stalk prerequisite. Requiring each stalk to be a local ring remains a condition defining locally ringed spaces, not a property of stalks of every sheaf of rings.

The split-fibred-category source uses an isomorphism of categories over C with inverse over C. The split-fibred-groupoid source identifies exactly that category-over-base isomorphism, in both cases strictly commuting with projection functors. Requiring both categories to be fibred, or the chosen Grothendieck construction to be strict, remains parent-specific; ordinary category-over-base isomorphism does not itself imply fibration.

Catenarity uses maximal finite strict chains of irreducible closed subsets between Y⊆Z, which first have exactly the same underlying Z_0⊊⋯⊊Z_n finite strict chain construction and length convention as Krull dimension of a space. The no-intermediate-set maximality condition, fixed endpoints, finite codimension and equality of maximal-chain lengths are extra parent constraints.

The category-fibred-in-sets source invokes the ordinary covariant functor p:E→C from total category to base category without assumed smallness. This is the same general identity/composition-preserving category functor prerequisite as the unrestricted F:C→D used in 2-categories and fibrations; p is merely a variable name. The cartesian-lift and discrete-fibre conditions remain parent-specific and are not imposed on all functors.
